chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a man who took ten arṭals of grape juice, so he poured twenty ritals of water over it and cooked it until twenty ritals from it evaporated and ten arṭals remained, is the drinking of that permissible or not? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever is cooked upon the third of it, so it is permissible.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for grape juice to become permissible (halal) as vinegar according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between *khamr* (intoxicant) and *khal* (vinegar) by establishing a quantitative threshold: cooking grape juice until one-third evaporates renders the remainder permissible. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on physical transformation (*istihlak*) as a mechanism for purifying substances, ensuring that the intoxicating property is sufficiently diminished or altered to be safe for consumption.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Uqba Bin Khalid,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding a man who took ten ratls (units of measurement) from the grape juice, so he poured twenty ratls of water over it and cooked it until twenty ratls from it evaporated and there remained ten ratls, is it correct to drink that or not?’ So heasws said: ‘Whatever is cooked upon the third of it, so it is Permissible’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah from ‘Uqbah ibn Khalid who has said the following:

“About the case of a man who takes ten ritl of grape juice, then pours in it twenty ritl of water, then boils it until twenty ritl of it is evaporated and only ten ritl is left; if it can be used for drink or not. He (the Imam) said, ‘What is cooked until only one-third remains it is lawful.’”
